akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿أَسْفَاراً﴾, and its singular is "السِّفْر".

akhfash:9-9.t:
And He said ﴿مِن يَوْمِ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ﴾: He means — and Allah knows best — "from the prayer of the day of Jumuʿa" (مِنْ صَلاةِ يَوْمِ الجُمُعَةِ).
Some grammarians said that "الأَسْفار" has no singular, like "أَبابيل" and "أَساطِير", and like the saying of the Arabs "ثَوْبٌ أكْبَاشٌ", which is a garment of poor spinning, and "ثَوْبٌ مِزْقٌ" for one that is torn to pieces. «[Translator's note: this second paragraph concerns ﴿أَسْفَاراً﴾ in verse 5, although in the source it stands in the entry for verse 9.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ﴾ declares Him transcendent — so the lām is redundant (zāʾida) — ﴿مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: in the mention of مَا there is a giving of predominance (taghlīb) to the majority; ﴿الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ﴾ the One declared transcendent above what does not befit Him, ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ in His dominion and His making.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ the Arabs — the ummī being one who neither writes nor reads a book — ﴿رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ﴾: he is Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ the Quran, ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purifies them from idolatry, ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ the rulings in it; ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: lightened from the heavy (inna), its ism being omitted, i.e. "and indeed they" ﴿كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ before his coming ﴿لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الْأُمِّيِّينَ, i.e. those present ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ and those coming of them after them, ﴿لَمَّا﴾ not ﴿يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ﴾ in precedence and merit. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His dominion and His making. They are the Followers (al-tābiʿūn); and limiting it to them suffices to show the merit of the Companions, among whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent, over everyone besides them to whom he was sent and who believed in him, of all humans and jinn until the Day of Resurrection, because every generation is better than the one following it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾: the Prophet and those mentioned with him; ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْرَاةَ﴾ were charged with acting upon it, ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا﴾ did not act upon what is in it of his ﷺ description, and so did not believe in him, ﴿كَمَثَلِ الْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًا﴾, i.e. books, in not benefiting from them. ﴿بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ that confirm the Prophet ﷺ — and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "this likeness". ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هَادُوا إِنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾: the two conditions are attached to تَمَنَّوُا, on the basis that the first is a restriction on the second, i.e. if you are truthful in your claim that you are the friends of Allah — and the friend (walī) prefers the Hereafter, whose beginning is death — then wish for it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ of their disbelief in the Prophet, which entails their being liars; ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ﴾ — the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) — ﴿مُلَاقِيكُمْ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَى عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ﴾ the secret and the open, ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوةِ مِنْ﴾ in the sense of فِي ﴿يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا﴾ go ﴿إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. the prayer, ﴿وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ﴾, i.e. leave off concluding it. ﴿ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better; so do it.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلَوةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: a command of permission; ﴿وَابْتَغُوا﴾ seek provision ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ with a remembrance ﴿كَثِيرًا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ succeed. He ﷺ was giving the sermon on Friday when a caravan arrived, and the drum was beaten for its arrival as was customary; so the people went out to it from the mosque except twelve men, and there was revealed:

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا﴾, i.e. the trade, because it was what they sought, not the amusement, ﴿وَتَرَكُوكَ﴾ in the sermon ﴿قَائِمًا قُلْ مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of reward ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ for those who believe ﴿مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجَارَةِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ﴾: it is said "every person provides for his household", i.e. from the provision of Allah the Exalted.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ما في السموات»; ﴿الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ badal (substitute) for the Name of Majesty.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿بَعَثَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَسُولًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا»; ﴿يَتْلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is a naʿt; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿آياتِهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يتلو»; ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ its second object; ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ conjoined to «الكتاب». ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿إِنْ كانُوا﴾ «إن» is lightened (mukhaffafa) [from «إنّ»], and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ both are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the lām is differentiating (fāriqa); ﴿في ضَلالٍ﴾ the khabar of «كانوا»; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ a naʿt, and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأميين»; ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «آخرين»; ﴿لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لمّا», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is a second naʿt of «آخرين»; ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿ذلِكَ فَضْلُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿يُؤْتِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿مَنْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الْفَضْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to the relative noun; ﴿حُمِّلُوا﴾ a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿التَّوْراةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the wāw being its fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْحِمارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause «مثل..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَحْمِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿أَسْفاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بِئْسَ﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb; ﴿مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ﴾ fāʿil, annexed to «القوم»; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «القوم»; ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿بِآياتِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْقَوْمِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi «[Translator's note: the quoted word is printed with a kasra in the source; in the verse it is «الْقَوْمَ», accusative.]»; ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ a naʿt of «القوم», and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is a badal (substitute) for «أيّها», and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿هادُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿زَعَمْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءُ﴾ «أنّ», its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أنّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «زعمتم»; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولياء»; ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ both are attached to «أولياء» as well; ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ «كان», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is initial, with no grammatical position. And the apodosis is omitted.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿لا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ﴾ «لا» is negating, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿قَدَّمَتْ﴾ a past verb; ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ both are attached to «عليم», and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «الموت»; ﴿تَفِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذي»; ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿مُلاقِيكُمْ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إنّ», and the clause «إن الموت..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿تُرَدُّونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلى عالِمِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَالشَّهادَةِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الغيب». ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to «تردون»; ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of «كنتم», and the clause «كنتم..» is the ṣila of «ما».

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿نُودِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; ﴿لِلصَّلاةِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿مِنْ يَوْمِ﴾ both are attached to the verb as well; ﴿الْجُمُعَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَاسْعَوْا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا», with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلى ذِكْرِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَذَرُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «فاسعوا»; ﴿الْبَيْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «خير»; ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional, making the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «كنتم», and the clause «كنتم..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. And the apodosis is omitted.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿إذا قُضِيَتِ﴾ «إذا» is an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive, and a passive past verb; ﴿الصَّلاةُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa). ﴿فَانْتَشِرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَابْتَغُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «فانتشروا»; ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ conjoined to «فانتشروا», the Name of Majesty being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object); ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ «لعلّ» and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «لعلّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِذا رَأَوْا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, «إذا» is an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿تِجارَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by iḍāfa; ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿لَهْواً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تجارة»; ﴿انْفَضُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿إِلَيْها﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿ما﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to the Name of Majesty; ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); ﴿مِنَ اللَّهْوِ﴾ both are attached to the khabar; ﴿وَمِنَ التِّجارَةِ﴾ conjoined to «من اللهو», and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «قل..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الرَّازِقِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقُدُّوسِ) with ḍamma on the qāf and doubling of the dāl, one of the names of Allah the Exalted; it may also take fatḥa [i.e. قَدُّوس], meaning the Pure or the Blessed. Every word on the pattern faʿūl has fatḥa, except قدوس, سبوح, ذرّوح and فرّوج, which take ḍamma and may also take fatḥa.
(أَسْفاراً) plural of سِفْر (with kasra on the sīn), which is a large book, because when it is read it "discloses" (yusfiru) and uncovers the meanings it contains.

* I'rab:
(يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ) يسبّح is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) with the object. ما is the fāʿil (agent), the majority being given precedence over the minority [i.e. ما, used for non-rational beings, is used to cover all]. في السموات is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; وما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات; and what follows are adjectives of, or a badal (substitute) from, الله.
(هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ) هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar (predicate); the clause بعث is the ṣila of الذي, and في الأميّين is attached to بعث. The meaning of الأميين has been discussed at length in Āl ʿImrān. رسولا is the object of بعث and منهم a naʿt (adjective) of رسولا.
(يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ) The clause يتلو is a second naʿt or a ḥāl (circumstantial); عليهم is attached to يتلو and آياته is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ويزكيهم is conjoined to يتلو; it is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ويعلمهم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi; الكتاب is a second mafʿūl bihi and الحكمة is conjoined to الكتاب.
(وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is lightened from the heavy [inna] and is inoperative (muhmala). كانوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw being its noun; من قبل is a ḥāl; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) which is specific to the lightened إن; في ضلال is the khabar of كانوا and مبين a naʿt of ضلال.
(وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction. آخرين is genitive (majrūr), conjoined to الأميّين, i.e. "and He sent him among others of the unlettered", or accusative (manṣūb), conjoined to the accusative pronoun in يعلمهم, i.e. "and He teaches others who have not joined them". منهم is a ḥāl of آخرين, i.e. the others being from the unlettered in general. لمّا is a particle of negation and jussive; يلحقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لمّا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt of آخرين. The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); هو is a mubtadaʾ, العزيز a first khabar and الحكيم a second khabar.
(ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ) ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the great matter, namely the Messenger and his people being favoured over others; فضل الله is the khabar. يؤتيه is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he"; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of ذلك. من is a second mafʿūl bihi and the clause يشاء is the ṣila of من. الله is a mubtadaʾ, ذو الفضل the khabar, and العظيم a naʿt of الفضل.
(مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement, set out to strike a parable for the Jews when they abandoned acting upon the Torah and did not believe in Muḥammad. مثل is a mubtadaʾ and الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause حملوا is the ṣila of الذين. حملوا is a passive past verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and التوراة is a second mafʿūl bihi. ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يحملوها is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi. The meaning of "carrying" (al-ḥaml) here is not carrying on the back; rather it is from ḥamāla (surety), and al-ḥamīl is the guarantor. The author of al-Mukhtār says: «ḥamala bi-dayn wa-diya (he bore a debt and a blood-money), of the pattern ḍaraba, ḥamālatan with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, i.e. he stood surety; ḥammalahu al-risālata taḥmīlan means he charged him with carrying it; and taḥammala al-ḥamālata means he bore it». كمثل الحمار is the khabar of مثل. The clause يحمل أسفارا is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of الجار [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الحمار» "the donkey"]. They have also permitted it to be in the position of genitive as a naʿt of الحمار, since it is treated like an indefinite noun, as what is meant by it is الحبس [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الجنس» "the genus"]; so it belongs to the same category as the poet's saying:
ولقد أمر على اللئيم يسبني ... فمضيت ثمت قلت لا يعنيني
(I pass by the base man who insults me, so I go on my way and say: he does not mean me.)
More discussion of this comparison will come in the section on rhetoric. أسفارا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ) بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; مثل القوم is the fāʿil of بئس and الذين an adjective; the clause كذبوا is the ṣila, and بآيات الله is attached to كذبوا. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "this parable".
(وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين a naʿt of القوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها كمثل الحمار يحمل أسفارا» there is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): He likened the Jews, inasmuch as they did not benefit from what the Torah contains by way of guidance to belief in Muḥammad ﷺ and allusion to his being sent, to the donkey that carries books and does not know what is in them. The point of resemblance is failing to benefit from what is present and existing: the donkey walks along its way sensing nothing of what it carries on its back except toil and fatigue; likewise the Jews read the Torah and memorised it, then turned away from the proofs and portents of the prophethood of Muḥammad son of ʿAbd Allāh that it contained.

dervis-irab:6-11.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هادُوا إِنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The i'rab of يا أيها الذين has been given many times. The clause هادوا is the ṣila (relative clause); it is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), i.e. they took Judaism as a religion. إن is conditional, and زعمتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). أنّ together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of زعمتم; أنّ and its noun, and أولياء الله is its khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source, though the Qur'anic wording is أولياء لله]; لله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أولياء, or to أولياء itself; من دون الناس is a second naʿt or a ḥāl (circumstantial). The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because it is a clause of request (ṭalabiyya); تمنّوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and الموت is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إن is conditional, then كان, its noun and its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then wish for it".
(وَلا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ أَبَداً بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and لا is negating; يتمنّونه is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi. أبدا is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to يتمنّونه. بما is attached to what the negation implies, since it is the cause of the negation of wishing; the clause قدّمت is the ṣila and أيديهم the fāʿil. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), عليم the khabar, and بالظالمين is attached to عليم.
(قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلاقِيكُمْ) قل is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "you". إنّ and its noun; الذي is a naʿt of الموت, the clause تفرّون is the ṣila, and منه is attached to تفرّون. The fāʾ is a linking one, because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun; إنّ and its noun, and ملاقيكم is its khabar; the clause فإنه ملاقيكم is the khabar of the first إنّ. A group, among them al-Farrāʾ, rejected this and made the fāʾ redundant (zāʾida). It has also been said that the khabar is الذي itself and what follows it is a new sentence (istiʾnāf), as if it were said: "Death is the thing that you flee from"; al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, and it is supported by the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī without the fāʾ.
(ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلى عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; تردّون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and إلى عالم الغيب is attached to تردّون. فينبئكم is conjoined to تردّون; بما is in the position of accusative as the second object of ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is a ṣila with no grammatical position, and the clause تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ) إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its protasis in the genitive [i.e. annexed to it] and made accusative by its apodosis. The clause نودي is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; للصلاة is attached to نودي. من يوم الجمعة is attached to an omitted ḥāl, since it serves as an explanation and clarification of إذا. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what is "من" in His saying من يوم الجمعة? I answer: it is an explanation (bayān) of إذا and a clarification of it». The discussion of al-Jumuʿa will come at length in the section on benefits. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «"من" means في», i.e. "on the day of Jumuʿa", so it would be attached to نودي. By the call (al-nidāʾ) here is meant the adhān. The fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; اسعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and إلى ذكر الله is attached to اسعوا. ذروا is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and البيع is the mafʿūl bihi.
(ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of hastening and abandoning preoccupation with worldly affairs; خير is the khabar and لكم is attached to خير. إن is conditional and كنتم the protasis; the clause تعلمون is the khabar of كنتم, and the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(فَإِذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, and the clause قضيت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; الصلاة is the nāʾib fāʿil. The fāʾ is linking; انتشروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position; في الأرض is attached to انتشروا. ابتغوا is conjoined to فانتشروا, and من فضل الله is attached to ابتغوا.
(وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) واذكروا is conjoined to فانتشروا; the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi; كثيرا is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or an adverb of time. لعلّ and its noun, and the clause تفلحون is its khabar.
(وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً) Conjoined to what precedes; the clause انفضّوا إليها has no grammatical position. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: how did He say إليها when He mentioned two things? I answer: its implied form is "When they saw merchandise they dispersed towards it, or amusement they dispersed towards it [masc.]", so one of the two was omitted because the one mentioned indicates it». تركوك is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; قائما is a second mafʿūl bihi, and it may also be parsed as a ḥāl. The clause تركوك قائما is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of انفضّوا, with قد implied; or you may make it conjoined in sequence to the clauses preceding it.
(قُلْ ما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجارَةِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ) ما is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila; خير is the khabar, and من اللهو is attached to خير; ومن التجارة is conjoined to من اللهو. الله is a mubtadaʾ and خير الرازقين the khabar.

* Benefits:
The generality of readers read الجمعة with two ḍammas, while Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥayyān [Translator's note: so in the source; the reader usually cited here is Abū Ḥaywa] and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read it with sukūn on the mīm (الجُمْعة). It has been said that this is a dialectal variant of the first, made quiescent for lightness, and that it is the dialect of Tamīm. It has also been said that it is a maṣdar meaning "gathering". And it has been said [Translator's note: the source prints «وقل», evidently for «وقيل»]: since it has the meaning of the verb, it became like رجل هُزْأة, i.e. one who is mocked; so since الجمعة carries the meaning of being gathered, it was made quiescent because it is semantically a patient (mafʿūl bihi) or resembles one. The Arabs used to call it al-ʿArūba. It has been said that Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy named it so because people gathered on it and to him. In al-Kashshāf: «It is said that the Anṣār said: the Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians likewise; so come, let us make a day for ourselves on which we gather, remember Allah and pray. They said: Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians, so make it the day of al-ʿArūba. So they gathered to Saʿd ibn Zurāra [Translator's note: so in the source; the Companion is usually named Asʿad ibn Zurāra], and he led them that day in two rakʿas and admonished them; and they named it the day of al-Jumuʿa because of their gathering on it. Then Allah revealed the verse of al-Jumuʿa. This was the first Jumuʿa held in Islam. As for the first Jumuʿa that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led: when he arrived in Medina as an emigrant, he stopped at Qubāʾ with Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf and stayed there on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then on Friday he set out heading for Medina, and the Jumuʿa prayer overtook him among Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf in the bed of a valley of theirs, so he delivered the sermon and prayed the Jumuʿa». It is related from one of them: Allah invalidated the claims of the Jews in three things: they boasted that they were the friends and beloved of Allah, so He gave them the lie in His saying «فتمنّوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين»; [they boasted] that they were the People of the Book while the Arabs had no book, so He likened them to the donkey carrying books; and [they boasted] of the Sabbath, and that the Muslims had nothing like it, so Allah legislated the Jumuʿa for them.
This being so, whoever wants more length and detail should consult the books of the Sunna and of fiqh, and the extended works of tafsīr.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱنتَشِرُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَٱبْتَغُواْ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
This is a permission and a licence: whoever wishes may sell, and whoever wishes may stay in the mosque.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً ٱنفَضُّوۤاْ إِلَيْهَا﴾.
He made the هاء [of إليها] refer to the trade and not to the amusement. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وإذا رأوا لهوا أو تجارة انفضوا إليها". They mention that the Prophet ﷺ was giving the sermon on Friday when Diḥya al-Kalbī arrived with a caravan of trade from Syria containing everything people needed; the drum was beaten to announce his arrival to the people, and all the people went out to him except eight persons. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً﴾, meaning the trade he arrived with, ﴿أَوْ لَهْواً﴾, meaning the beating of the drum. Had it been said: انفضوا إليه, meaning the amusement, it would be correct, as He said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً﴾ and did not say: بها. And had it been said: بهما and انفضوا إليهما, as He said: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقِيراً فاللهُ أولى بهِمَا﴾, it would be correct. Better than that in Arabic is to make the referring pronoun go back to the last of the two nouns; and what is beyond that is permissible.
[Translator's note: the source text has «فقد دحية» ("Diḥya lost"); the sense is clearly «فقدم دحية» ("Diḥya arrived"), and it is translated accordingly.]
إليها was chosen — in our reading and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh — only because the trade was more important to them, and they were more delighted with it than with the beating of the drum, since the drum only pointed to it; so the whole meaning is for it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِمْ﴾.
It is said that they are those who did not become Muslim in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then became Muslim; and it is said: they are those who come afterwards. (وآخرين) is in the position of the genitive: He sent [a messenger] among the unlettered and among others of them. And if you made it accusative by His saying: ﴿ويُزَكِّيهِمْ ويُعَلِّمُهُم﴾ — "and teaches others" — it would be accusative by being joined back to the هاء in يزكيهم and يعلمهم.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَثَلِ ٱلْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَاراً﴾.
يحمل is a ṣila (qualifying clause) of الحمار, because it is in the manner of an indefinite noun; if you put حاملا in place of يحمل, you would say: كمثل الحمار حاملا أسفارا. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: كمثل حمار يحمل أسفارا. السِّفْر is the singular of الأسفار, which are large books. He likens the Jews, and whoever did not become Muslim, since they did not benefit from the Torah and the Gospel — and these two are proofs of the Prophet ﷺ — to the donkey that carries books of knowledge and does not know what is on it.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْمَوْتَ ٱلَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ﴾.
The Arabs have put the فاء in the khabar (predicate) of (إنّ) because it fell upon الذى, and الذى is a word that takes a ṣila (relative clause). The Arabs put the فاء in every khabar whose noun is one of those that take a ṣila, such as من and الذى; and omitting it is correct. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "إن الموتَ الذى تفرُّون منه ملاقيكُم". Whoever puts in the فاء takes الذى in the sense of a conditional (jazāʾ), since it needs to be completed by a ṣila; and whoever omits the فاء follows the regular rule (qiyās), because you say: إن أخاك قائم (your brother is standing), and you do not say: إن أخاك فقائم. But if you said: إن ضاربك فظالم (the one who strikes you is unjust), it would be permissible, because the import of إن ضاربك is like your saying: إن من يضربك فظالم. So by analogy with this, put the فاء for any single noun that carries the sense of a conditional.
Some of the commentators said: [the meaning is] death is that which you flee from, so they made الذى stand in the position of the khabar of الموت; then He said: whether you flee or do not flee, it will meet you. You will not find this tenable in Arabic, and Allah knows best what is right in that.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿مِن يَوْمِ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash lightened it, saying: الْجُمْعة, and ʿĀṣim and the people of the Ḥijāz made it heavy [الجُمُعة]. There is also a dialect form: جُمَعَة, the dialect of Banū ʿUqayl; had it been read so, it would be correct. Those who say الجُمَعة take it as a description of the day, that it is a day of gathering (yawm jumaʿa), as you say رجل ضُحَكة of one who laughs a lot.
[Translator's note: the source has «خفضها» ("put it in the genitive"); in context this must mean "lightened it" (khaffafahā), i.e. read it with sukūn, and is translated so.]
His saying: ﴿فَٱسْعَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "فامضوا إلى ذكر الله". Going (al-muḍiyy), striving (al-saʿy) and going (al-dhahāb) have one meaning, for you say of a man: هو يسعى فى الأرض يبتغى من فضل الله (he goes about in the land seeking of Allah's bounty), and this does not mean running hard.
One of the imams said: If I read it "فاسعوا", I would run hard — he means: I would hurry. The Arabs make saʿy faster than muḍiyy. But the [correct] view on it is the first view.
His saying: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ٱلْبَيْعَ﴾.
When He ordered leaving off selling, He ordered leaving off buying, because the buyer and the seller are both called al-bayyiʿān. So when the muezzin calls to prayer on Friday, selling and buying are forbidden [199/a].

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «الملك» and what follows it are naʿts (adjectives) of the Divine Name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولا»; the clause «يتلو» is a second naʿt; «الكتاب» is a second object; the wāw in «وإن» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «إن» is lightened from the heavy [إنَّ] and inoperative (muhmala), and the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); the preposition and its genitive noun «من قبل» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun of kāna.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: His words «وآخرين»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {الأُمِّيِّينَ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آخرين»; the clause «لما يلحقوا» is a naʿt of «آخرين»; and the clause «وهو العزيز» is conjoined to the resumptive clause {هُوَ الَّذِي}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «يؤتيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فضل الله»; the clause «والله ذو الفضل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «ثم لم يحملوها» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «حُمِّلوا»; the preposition and its genitive noun «كمثل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مثل»; the clause «يحمل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; the clause «بئس مثل» is resumptive, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: «بئس مثل القوم مثل الذين كذبوا» (evil is the likeness of the people, the likeness of those who denied); «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «القوم»; the clause «والله لا يهدي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «زعم»; the preposition and its genitive noun «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولياء», and likewise (مِنْ دُونِهِ); the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ولا يتمنونه» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «والله عليم بالظالمين»; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The fāʾ in «فإنه» is redundant (zāʾida); it entered because the noun includes the meaning of a condition, and the ruling on what is qualified by a relative noun is the ruling on the relative noun in this respect; the clause «إنه ملاقيكم» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause «ثم تردُّون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar of «إن», the linking element being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: after it (بعده); and the clause «فينبئكم» is conjoined to the clause «تردون».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «الذين» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the conditional clause, the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «من يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصلاة»; the clause «ذلكم خير» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to «خير»; the clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it; and the clause «ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذروا»; «كثيرا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the clause «لعلكم تفلحون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; with conjunction by «أو» the pronoun is not put in the dual, because it is for one of two things; the pronoun of «التجارة» rather than «اللهو» was used for emphasis [of importance]; the clause «وتركوك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; «قائما» is a ḥāl; «ما» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «خير» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من اللهو» is attached to «خير».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, Exalted is He, يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِم آيَاته ويزكيهم وَيُعلمهُم: all of them are naʿts (adjectives) of رسول; likewise منهم is also a naʿt. All of them are in the position of the accusative.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying وآخرين مِنْهُم: in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الأميين. It is also said: in the position of the accusative by conjunction with the accusative latent pronoun in يعلمهم or يزكيهم. It is also said that it is conjoined to the meaning of يتلو عليهم, because its meaning is "He makes them know His signs".
His saying لما يلْحقُوا: the origin of لمّا is لم, to which ما was added so that it would negate what is near to the present; had ما not been with it, it would be a negation of the past and nothing else. When you say لم يقم زيد ("Zayd did not stand"), it is a negation for one who said قام زيد ("Zayd stood"); and when you say لما يقم زيد ("Zayd has not yet stood"), it is a negation for one who said قد قام زيد ("Zayd has just stood").

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying يحمل أسفارا: يحمل is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحمار.
His saying بئس مثل الْقَوْم: مثل is nominative by بئس, and the clause is in the position of the explanation of an omitted clause; its implied form is "wretched is the likeness of the people — this likeness" (بئس مثل القوم هذا المثل), but it was omitted because the speech indicates it.
His saying فإنه ملاقيكم: this is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The فاء entered the khabar of إنّ only because its noun has been described by الذي, and the adjective is the thing described; الذي is vague, and vagueness is one of the defining features of a condition; so the فاء entered the khabar because of the vagueness in الذي, which is one of the features of a condition. That is good because الذي is completed by a verb; had it been completed by something other than a verb, the entry of the فاء into the khabar would not be permissible. Were you to say إن أخاك فجالس, it would not be permissible, since there is nothing vague in the speech. It is also possible that الذي تفرون منه is the khabar, and the فاء in فإنه ملاقيكم is the answer to the clause, as you say زيد منطلق فقم إليه ("Zayd is leaving, so go to him").

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying يَوْم الْجُمُعَة: making the ميم quiescent [الجُمْعة] is permissible, for lightness; it is also said that it is a dialect form. It is also said that, since it contains the sense of the verb, it became like رجل هُزْأة, i.e. one who is mocked; so, since الجمعة contains the sense of gathering, it was made quiescent, because it is an object in meaning or resembles it, so it became like هزأة for the one who is mocked. In it there is a third dialect form, الجُمَعة with a fatḥa on the ميم, attributing the action to it, as if it gathers people, as one says رجل لُحَنة when he attributes errors of speech to people, and قُرَأة when he teaches people to recite.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يسبح لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض الملك القدوس العزيز الحكيم﴾: يسبح is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); in لله the lām is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, or the lām is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) on the object; ما is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿في السماوات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to something omitted which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿ما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾; and what follows it are adjectives (ṣifāt), or a badal (substitute) from الله.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿هو الذي بعث في الأميين رسولا منهم﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause بعث is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position. في الأميين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بعث﴾; رسولًا is the object of بعث; and منهم is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رسولًا﴾.
﴿يتلو عليهم آياته ويزكيهم ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة﴾: the clause يتلو is a second naʿt or a ḥāl (circumstantial); عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يتلو﴾; آياته is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يزكيهم is conjoined to يتلو, and it is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and a mafʿūl bihi; يعلمهم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil, and a first mafʿūl bihi; الكتاب is the second mafʿūl bihi; and الحكمة is conjoined to الكتاب.
﴿وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is lightened from the heavy [إنّ] and is inoperative (muhmala); كانوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun (ism); من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) that is particular to the lightened إن; في ضلال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كانوا; and مبين is a naʿt of ﴿ضلال﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; آخرين is genitive (majrūr) by conjunction with الأميين, or accusative (manṣūb) by conjunction with the accusative pronoun in يعلمهم, i.e. "and He teaches others who have not joined them"; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from آخرين; لما is a particle of negation and jussive; يلحقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لما﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آخرين﴾; and بهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يلحقوا﴾.
﴿وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject); العزيز is the first khabar (predicate) and الحكيم the second khabar; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and فضل الله is the khabar (predicate); يؤتيه is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a second khabar of ذلك; من is the second mafʿūl bihi; and the clause يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿والله ذو الفضل العظيم﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ; ذو الفضل is the khabar; and العظيم is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الفضل﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿مثل الذين حملوا التوراة ثم لم يحملوها﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; مثل is the mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين is a relative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿حُمِّلُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position; حملوا is a past verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); التوراة is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يحملوها is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and ﴿ها﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿كمثل الحمار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of مثل.
﴿يحمل أسفارًا﴾: the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الحمار; it has also been said: in the position of a genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الحمار; and أسفارًا is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿بئس مثل القوم الذين كذبوا بآيات الله﴾: بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; مثل القوم is the fāʿil of بئس; الذين is an adjective (ṣifa); the clause كذبوا is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كذبوا﴾; and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "this likeness".
﴿والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi; and الظالمين is a naʿt of ﴿القوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت).
﴿يا أيها الذين هادوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; the clause هادوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; هادوا is a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; its meaning: they took Judaism as a religion.
﴿إن زعمتم أنكم أولياء لله من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين﴾: إن is conditional; زعمتم is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أن together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of زعمتم; أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿كم﴾ is its noun (ism), and أولياء لله is its khabar (predicate); in لله the lām is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أولياء﴾, or to أولياء itself; من دون الناس is a second naʿt, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a clause of request (ṭalabiyya); تمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; الموت is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إن is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and صادقين is its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then wish for it".

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ولا يتمنونه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يتمنونه is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أبدًا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتمنونه﴾.
﴿بما قدمت أيديهم﴾: بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what is in the sense of negation, because it is the cause of the negation of the wishing; the clause ﴿قدمت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. أيديهم is the fāʿil.
﴿والله عليم بالظالمين﴾: الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); عليم is the khabar (predicate); and بالظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليم﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "you" (أنت).
﴿إن الموت الذي تفرون منه فإنه ملاقيكم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and الموت is its noun (ism); الذي is a relative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a naʿt (adjective) of الموت; the clause ﴿تَفِرُّون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تفرون﴾; the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun; إن is an abrogating particle, the hāʾ is its noun, and ملاقيكم is its khabar (predicate); and the clause ﴿فإنه ملاقيكم﴾ is the khabar of the first إن. It has also been said: the fāʾ in ﴿فإنه﴾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant). And it has been said: ﴿الذي﴾ is the khabar of إنّ, and the clause ﴿فإنه ملاقيكم﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; تردون is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلى عالم الغيب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تردون﴾; فينبئكم is conjoined to تردون; بما is in the place of an accusative as the second object of ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. And the clause تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة﴾: إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of future time, putting its condition in the genitive and made accusative by its apodosis; the clause ﴿نودي﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; للصلاة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نودي﴾; من يوم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الصلاة﴾. الجمعة is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; اسعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); إلى ذكر الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اسعوا﴾; ذروا is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and البيع is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون﴾: ذلكم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خير﴾; إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause تعلمون is the khabar of كنتم; and the apodosis of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb (ẓarf) that includes the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انتشروا﴾; the clause قضيت is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) through the adverb's being annexed to it; الصلاة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); انتشروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿انتشروا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿انتشروا﴾; ابتغوا is conjoined to ﴿فانتشروا﴾; and من فضل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ابتغوا﴾.
﴿واذكروا الله كثيرا﴾: اذكروا is conjoined to ﴿فانتشروا﴾; the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and كثيرًا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or an adverb of time.
﴿لعلكم تفلحون﴾: لعل is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope (tarajjī); ﴿كم﴾ is its noun (ism); and the clause تفلحون is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وإذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها وتركوك قائما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ﴿إذا﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) that includes the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انفضوا﴾; ﴿رأوا﴾ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿تجارة﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; ﴿لهوًا﴾ is conjoined to تجارة; ﴿انفضوا﴾ is a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil; ﴿إليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿انفضوا﴾; the clause ﴿انفضوا إليها﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; in ﴿وتركوك﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and تركوك is a past verb, the wāw of the group is the fāʿil, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; ﴿قائمًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of ﴿تركوك﴾, which is the kāf; and the clause ﴿تركوك قائمًا﴾ is conjoined to the apodosis clause ﴿انفضوا﴾, with no grammatical position. Or the wāw in ﴿وتركوك﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause ﴿وتركوك قائما﴾ is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of ﴿انفضوا﴾.
﴿قل ما عند الله خير من اللهو ومن التجارة والله خير الرازقين﴾: ﴿قل﴾ is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عند﴾ is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿خير﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿من اللهو﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خير﴾; ﴿ومن التجارة﴾ is conjoined to ﴿من اللهو﴾; ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, ﴿خير﴾ is the khabar, and ﴿الرازقين﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t: يُسَبِّحُ may refer to the future and the present. الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ: naʿt (adjective), and it carries the meaning of praise. The accusative is permissible outside the Qurʾān in the meaning of "I mean"; the nominative is permissible on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible without anything implied: you make it nominative as the mubtadaʾ, with الذي as the khabar (predicate). The implied form may be "He is the King, the Holy", with الَّذِي a naʿt of الملك. If you use the genitive, هُوَ is nominative as the mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي is its khabar; and «هو» may be nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of what is in الحكيم, with «الذي» a naʿt of الحكيم. بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولًا مِنْهُمْ is included in the ṣila (relative clause). يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "reciting to them", a naʿt of رسول. وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ: the meaning of يزكيهم is that he calls them to obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; when they obey Him they have been purified and he has purified them. وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ: assimilating the lām into the lām is permissible.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ is in the position of a genitive because it is conjoined to الأميين; it may be in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «هم» in يعلّمهم or to «هم» in يزكيهم; and it may be conjoined to the sense of يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ, i.e. he makes it known to them. لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ: Ibn Zayd said:
i.e. for whoever comes of the Arabs and non-Arabs until the Day of Resurrection; and Mujāhid said: for whoever followed after them, of all people. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest of what has been said about it, because the verse is general. لمّا is «لم» to which «ما» has been added for emphasis. Sībawayh said: «لمّا» is the answer to whoever says "he has done" (qad faʿala), and «لم» is the answer to whoever says "he did" (faʿala). Abū Jaʿfar said: except that what governs the jussive, according to all, is لم, and for that reason the nūn is dropped. وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ: whoever makes the hāʾ quiescent [Translator's note: i.e. wa-hwa] says: the ḍamma is heavy, and the word has been joined to what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ i.e. that which these have been given is a bounty from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, which He gives to whom He wills. وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ i.e. He is not blamed for diverting it from whomever He diverts it, because He has not withheld from him a right that he had with Him, nor wronged him by withholding it from him; rather, He knew that someone else was more deserving of it than he, so He diverted it to him.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ i.e. they were charged with upholding it and stopping at what is in it. ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها i.e. they did not do that. كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً: «يحمل» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "carrying". If it is said: how is this permissible, when one does not say جاءني غلام هند مسرعة? The answer is that the meaning is "their likeness is the likeness of those who were charged with the Torah" [Translator's note: so in the source]. The Kufans claimed that يحمل is a ṣila of الحمار, because it is in the status of an indefinite, and they call the naʿt of an indefinite a ṣila; then they contradicted this and said: the meaning is "like the likeness of the donkey, carrying books". بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ i.e. "this likeness"; then "this" was omitted because it has already been mentioned. وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ: the meaning is that He does not grant them success nor guide them aright, since it was in His knowledge that they would not believe; and it is said: He does not guide them to the reward.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ هادُوا: one says هاد يهود when he repents and when he returns. إِنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِياءُ لِلَّهِ مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ i.e. other than you. فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ i.e. if you are truthful that you are [His] friends — for He does not punish His friends — then wish for it, so that you find rest from the distress of this world, its cares and its griefs, and go on to the repose of Paradise.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَلا يَتَمَنَّوْنَهُ أَبَداً: and it was true, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said, and they refrained from that. بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ i.e. of sins. وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ i.e. possessing knowledge of whoever has wronged himself and ruined and destroyed himself through disbelief.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ i.e. which you refuse to wish for. الَّذِي is in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of الموت. فَإِنَّهُ مُلاقِيكُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. The entry of the fāʾ is permissible — whereas إنّ أخاك فمنطلق is not permissible — because the sentence carries the meaning of requital (jazāʾ). The Kufans permitted إنّ ضاربك فظالم, because according to them the sentence carries the meaning of requital. There is another view on it: that الذي تفرون منه is the khabar of إنّ — "death is that from which you flee". ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلى عالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ: a sentence conjoined to a sentence. فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ is conjoined to تردون.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
Al-Aʿmash read الْجُمُعَةِ with the mīm quiescent [al-jumʿa], and the dialect of the Banū ʿUqayl is «من يوم الجمعة» with fatḥa on the mīm [al-jumaʿa]. [Translator's note: the print shows al-jumuʿa in both places.] Whoever reads الْجُمُعَةِ [al-jumʿa] explains it in several ways. Among them: the original is al-jumuʿa, and then the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness. It may be that this is a dialect with the same meaning as that. And a third answer: it is made quiescent because the assembling takes place in it, so it resembles the object, just as one says رجل هزأة, i.e. one who is laughed at, and لحنة, i.e. one whose speech is corrected. Whoever says الْجُمُعَةِ [al-jumaʿa] attributes the action to it, i.e. it assembles people, just as one says رجل لحنة, i.e. he corrects people's speech, and قراء, i.e. he teaches people to recite. فَاسْعَوْا إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: Qatāda said: i.e. with your hearts and your deeds, i.e. proceed. وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ: in the past tense one does not say وذر. Sībawayh said: they made do with ترك instead of it; and someone else said: because the wāw is heavy, so they turned to ترك, since it has its meaning. ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ i.e. hastening to the remembrance of Allah. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: and it is the sermon — better for you than buying and selling.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: when the sun passes the meridian, buying and selling become forbidden; and someone else said: the apparent sense of the Qurʾān shows that that is when the muezzin calls the adhān while the imam is on the pulpit. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ what holds your benefit and your harm.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
I.e. the Friday prayer. فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ i.e. if you wish — what precedes it shows that — and the exegetes said: it is a permission. In the ḥadīth from Anas ibn Mālik, traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ. Abū Jaʿfar said: for visiting a sick person, or attending a funeral, or visiting, i.e. for the sake of Allah. [Translator's note: the attribution "Abū Jaʿfar said" appears in the source in the middle of the ḥadīth's explanation, as printed.]
The apparent sense of the verse shows the permissibility of dispersing in the land to seek provision in this world or reward in the Hereafter. وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً i.e. for what [He has bestowed] upon you [Translator's note: the source reads لما عليكم; a verb such as أنعم appears to be missing] and the success He has granted you. لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ i.e. you will enter Paradise and abide in it; and al-falāḥ is permanence.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها: the scholars differed about the "amusement" (al-lahw) here. Sulaymān ibn Bilāl narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad from his father from Jābir, who said: when a woman was given in marriage, the pipes would be played for her and people would rush to it; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down this. Mujāhid said: the lahw is the drum. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is nearer to correctness, because Jābir witnessed the revelation. Al-Farrāʾ inclined to the second view because, according to what he mentioned, when a caravan of trade arrived they would beat a drum for it and people would rush to it; and al-Farrāʾ relied in his book on the meanings [i.e. Maʿānī l-Qurʾān] on al-Kalbī, and al-Kalbī is abandoned in ḥadīth. As for His saying, Majestic and Mighty, انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها, and He did not say إليهما, its implied form according to the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is "and when they saw trade they dispersed to it"; then the second was conjoined to the first and entered into what it entered into. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the preferred thing is for the pronoun to refer back to the second; had it been as he said, it would have been انفضوا إليه; but he argues in this that what is intended is the trade. All of this is permissible: that it refer back to the first, or to the second, or to both. He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً
[al-Nisāʾ: 112], where the pronoun refers back to the second; and He, Majestic and Mighty, said: إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيراً فَاللَّهُ أَوْلى بِهِما [al-Nisāʾ: 135], where it refers back to both of them together. وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. standing delivering the sermon. قُلْ ما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجارَةِ i.e. what He has of reward.
وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ i.e. so ask Him alone, and turn in longing to Him alone, that He may give you ample provision.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(يسبّح للَّه ... في الأرض) its i'rab, in words and clauses, has been given [Note: in verse (1) of the preceding Sūrat al-Ṣaff.]. (الملك، القدوس، العزيز، الحكيم) are genitive naʿts (adjectives) of the word of majesty (Allah).

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأمّيّين) is attached to (بعث), the verb being given the sense of "raised/established" (أقام). (منهم) is attached to an adjective of (رسولا). (عليهم) is attached to (يتلو). (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places, and the fourth is a ḥāl (circumstantial) wāw. (إن) is the lightened form of the heavy (إنّ), and the ism (noun) of inna is omitted, i.e.: "they" (إنّهم). (قبل) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of a genitive, attached to a ḥāl from ضلال. (في ضلال) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of كانوا..
The clause «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «بعث ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «يتلو ... » is in the position of an accusative second naʿt of (رسولا) [Note: or a ḥāl from (رسولا).].
The clause «يزكّيهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «يعلّمهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «إن كانوا ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl.
The clause «كانوا ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the lightened inna.
3- (الواو) is a conjunction in the two places. (آخرين) is conjoined to الأمّيّين and is genitive. (منهم) is attached to a naʿt of (آخرين) [Note: or a ḥāl from آخرين, because it indicates the generality of the unlettered (al-ummiyyīn).], and the pronoun in it refers to الأمّيّين. (لمّا) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive. (بهم) is attached to (يلحقوا)..
The clause «لمّا يلحقوا ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from آخرين.
The clause «هو العزيز ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هو الذي [Note: or a ḥāl from the agent of بعث.] ...
4- The demonstrative in (ذلك) refers to the preference of the Messenger and his people. (من) is a relative noun in the position of an accusative second direct object. (الواو) is a conjunction - or a ḥāl wāw. (ذو) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (اللَّه)..
The clause «ذلك فضل اللَّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يؤتيه ... » is in the position of a nominative second khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك [Note: or a ḥāl from (فضل اللَّه), the operator in it being the sense of the demonstrative.].
The clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «اللَّه ذو الفضل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ذلك فضل [Note: or a ḥāl from the agent of يؤتيه.]..

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) is a conjunction. (كمثل) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (مثل)..
The specified object of censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "this parable". (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of a genitive naʿt of القوم. (بآيات) is attached to (كذّبوا). (الواو) is resumptive. (لا) is a negation.
The clause «مثل الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «حمّلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لم يحملوها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يحمل ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from الحمار [Note: or in the position of a genitive naʿt of حمار, because the (ال) in it is generic.].
The clause «بئس مثل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اللَّه لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «لا يهدي القوم ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).

* Morphology:
(أسفارا) is the plural of سفر, a name for a large book; its pattern is فعل (with kasra then sukūn), and the pattern of أسفار is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
The representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī) in the words of Allah the Exalted مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً. He likened the Jews - in that they are the bearers of the Torah, its readers and the preservers of what is in it, and yet they do not act upon it nor benefit from its verses, for it contains the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the glad tidings of him, and they did not believe in him - to a donkey carrying asfār, that is, large books of the books of learning: it walks with them and knows nothing of them except what passes over its sides and back of toil and fatigue. Everyone who has knowledge and does not act upon his knowledge, this is his likeness.

safi-cedvel:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) is an indefinite specified vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of an accusative badal (substitute) for أيّ - or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). (زعمتم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive, being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (للَّه) is attached to (أولياء) [Note: or attached to a naʿt of أولياء.. The interpreted maṣdar (أنّكم أولياء..) is in the position of an accusative, filling the place of the two objects of زعمتم.]. (من دون) is attached to (أولياء) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in أولياء.]. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive, being the protasis..
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «النداء ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «هادوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن زعمتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «تمنّوا ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, joined by fāʾ.
The clause «إن كنتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the response to the vocative [Note: The first condition in this construction is a restriction on the second, and that is the basic order, i.e.: "if you are truthful, if you claim that you are friends of Allah, then wish for death."]. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by the apodosis of the first condition, i.e.: "then wish for death."
7- (الواو) is resumptive in the two places. (لا) is a negation. (أبدا) is an adverb of time in the accusative, attached to the negated (يتمنّونه). (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it being its ṣila.]. (بالظالمين) is attached to (عليم)..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قدّمت ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the negated (يتمنّونه), and the (الباء) is causal.
The clause «لا يتمنّونه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «قدّمت أيديهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما). The clause «اللَّه عليم بالظالمين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
8- (منه) is attached to (تفرّون). (الفاء) is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of inna, because the ism was described by a relative and so took the ruling of the relative that resembles a condition. (ثمّ) is a conjunction, and the wāw in (تردّون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (إلى عالم) is attached to (تردّون). (بما كنتم) is like بما قدّمت..
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الموت ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «تفرّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «إنّه ملاقيكم ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of the (first) inna.
The clause «تردّون ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar of inna, the connector being implied, i.e. "you will be returned after it".
The clause «ينبئكم» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause تردّون.
The clause «كنتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of an accusative khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) is like يأيّها الذين هادوا [Note: in verse (6) of this sūra.]. (للصلاة) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (من يوم) is attached to a ḥāl from الصلاة. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (إلى ذكر) is attached to (اسعوا). (لكم) is attached to (خير)..
The clause «النداء ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الشرط وفعله وجوابه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «نودي للصلاة ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اسعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ذروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اسعوا.
The clause «ذلكم خير لكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption - or causal. The clause «كنتم تعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "if you know that it is better for you, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah."
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of an accusative khabar of كنتم.
10- (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the second is the connector of the apodosis. (في الأرض) is attached to (انتشروا). (من فضل) is attached to (ابتغوا). (كثيرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its description..
The clause «قضيت الصلاة ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «انتشروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ابتغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause انتشروا.
The clause «اذكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause انتشروا.
The clause «لعلّكم تفلحون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «تفلحون ... » is in the position of a nominative khabar of لعلّكم.
11- (الواو) is resumptive. (أو) is a conjunction. (إليها) is attached to (انفضّوا). (الواو) is a ḥāl wāw - or a conjunction. (قائما) is an accusative ḥāl from the address pronoun in (تركوك). (ما) is a relative noun in the position of a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (خير). (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to the implied ṣila of ما. (من اللهو) is attached to (خير), and likewise (من التجارة). (الواو) is resumptive..
The clause «رأوا ... » is in the position of a genitive muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «انفضّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تركوك ... » is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent of انفضّوا, with an implied قد [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause انفضّوا.].
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ما عند اللَّه خير ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying.
The clause «اللَّه خير الرازقين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(9) الجمعة: the name of one of the days of the week. Its origin is that it is a maṣdar meaning "gathering" (ijtimāʿ); its pattern is فعلة with two ḍammas» .
(اسعوا): it has an elision (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf), as is the case with the imperfect يسعون.. See verse (33) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.

* Benefits:
The Friday prayer..
This verse yields a juristic ruling, namely the obligation of answering the call on Friday. For this reason the jurists said that the Friday prayer is valid only in a mosque, and whoever misses it prays it as Ẓuhr.
