It also yields the prohibition of occupying oneself with other things after the call, by which is meant the adhān before the preacher; as for occupying oneself after the first adhān, it is disliked (makrūh). On the authority of Ibn Sīrīn, who said: The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet ﷺ arrived and before the Friday prayer was revealed; they are the ones who named it al-Jumuʿa. They said: The Jews have the day of Saturday and the Christians the day of Sunday, so let us make a day on which we gather, remember the name of Allah the Exalted and pray. So they made it the day of al-ʿArūba. Then Allah the Exalted revealed concerning that: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ. And Asʿad ibn Zurāra, may Allah be pleased with him, was the first to gather the people on Friday, and they were forty. Abū Dāwūd recorded it. As for the first Friday prayer that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held with his Companions, the biographers (ahl al-siyar) mention that when the Prophet ﷺ entered Medina as an emigrant, he stayed at Qubāʾ with Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, on Monday, twelve nights having passed of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, when the forenoon had extended. He stayed at Qubāʾ from Monday to Thursday and founded their mosque, which is the first mosque in Islam. Then he went out on Friday toward Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him among Banū Sālim ibn ʿAwf, in the bottom of their valley, where they had made a mosque in that place; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held the Friday prayer in it and delivered the sermon.
The number by which the Friday prayer is validly held:
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad and Isḥāq said:
The Friday prayer is not validly held with fewer than forty men of full qualification, that is, that they be free, of age, sane, and resident in a place which they do not leave in winter or summer except for a need. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz stipulated the presence of a ruler (wālī) for the validity of the Friday prayer. As for al-Shāfiʿī, he said: it is valid without a ruler. Abū Ḥanīfa said: the Friday prayer is held with four, on condition of the presence of a ruler. al-Awzāʿī and Abū Yūsuf said: it is held with three if a ruler is among them. al-Ḥasan said: it is held with two, like the rest of the prayers. Rabīʿa said: it is held with twelve men. The number is not completed by those on whom the Friday prayer is not obligatory, such as the slave, the woman, the traveller and the boy. It is held only in one place; but if the people are many and the congregational mosque is too narrow, the majority of jurists hold that it may be held in more than one congregational mosque. And Allah knows best.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الملك}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean the genitive «الملِكِ», with what follows it as a naʿt (adjective) of it; a badal (substitute) is weak because of their being derived forms. Abū Wāʾil, Maslama ibn Muḥārib and Ruʾba read it with the nominative ending, with an implied mubtadaʾ requiring praise. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And if it were read in the accusative, on the pattern of their saying «الحمدُ الله أهلَ الحَمْد», that would be a possible reading." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «القَدُّوس» with fatḥa on the qāf. The discussion of it, and of «الأمِّيِّ» and its plural «الأمِّيِّين», has already been given. And «يَتْلُوا» and what follows are ṣifas (qualifiers) of «رسول».

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {وَآخَرِينَ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is genitive by ʿaṭf (conjunction) on «الأمِّيِّيْنَ», that is: "and He sent among others of the unlettered." And {لَمَّا يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِمْ} is a ṣifa of the preceding «آخرين». The second is that it is accusative by ʿaṭf on the accusative pronoun in «يُعَلِّمُهم», that is: "and He teaches others who have not yet joined them, but will join them." Everyone who learns the law of Muḥammad ﷺ until the end of time has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as his teacher in potentiality (bi-l-quwwa), because he is the source of that great good and weighty virtue.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {حُمِّلُواْ التوراة}: this is the reading of the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «حَمَلوا», lightened, in the active.
His saying {كَمَثَلِ الحمار}: this is the reading of the majority. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «حِمارٍ» indefinite. It is equivalent in force to the reading of the others, because by «الحمار» the genus is meant. For this reason it was qualified by the clause after it, as will come. Al-Maʾmūn ibn Hārūn al-Rashīd read «يُحَمَّلُ» with shadda, in the passive. The clause «يَحْمِلُ» or «يُحْمَّلُ» has two possibilities: the first, which is the well-known one, is that it is in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحمار»; the second is that it is in the position of a ṣifa (qualifier) for «الحمار», because it behaves like an indefinite, since the genus is meant by it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "or genitive as a qualifier, because «الحمار» is like «اللئيم» in his saying:
4261 - ولَقد أَمُرُّ على اللئيمِ يَسُبُّني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And indeed I pass by the base man who curses me...)
This has been set out already, and that from it, in the view of some, is {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ} [Yā Sīn: 37], and that «نَسْلَخُ» is a naʿt of «الليل». The majority make it a ḥāl because of the formal definiteness. As for the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, the clause is only a qualifier, and it is not impossible, in the view of Sībawayh, that it be a ḥāl.
الأَسْفار is the plural of سِفْر, which is a book of gathered leaves.
His saying {بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القوم}: there are several possibilities. The first, which is the apparent and well-known one, is that «مَثَلُ القوم» is the agent of «بِئْس». And the one specified for blame is the relative noun after it. That poses a difficulty, because there must be agreement in reference between the agent of niʿma and biʾsa and the one specified, and here the "likeness" is not the denying people. The answer is that there is an omitted muḍāf, that is: بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القومِ مَثَلُ الذين كَذَّبوا. The second is that «الذين» is a ṣifa of «القوم», so that it is genitive in position, and the one specified for blame is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: "evil is the likeness of the denying people, the likeness of these"; and this is close to the first. The third is that the agent is omitted, and that «مَثَلُ القومِ» is the one specified for blame, its implied form being: بِئْسَ المَثَلُ مَثَلُ القوم, with the relative noun again a naʿt of «القوم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words incline to this, for he said: "The implied form is: بِئْسَ المَثَلُ مَثَلُ القومِ." This is invalid, because the agent is not omitted in the view of the Basrans except in three places, of which this is not one, unless one adopts the view of the Kufans. The fourth is that the tamyīz (specification) is omitted and the agent that it explains is latent, its implied form being: بئس مَثَلاً مَثَلُ القوم. Al-Zamakhsharī's words incline to this, for he said: "«بئْسَ مَثَلاً مَثَلُ القوم»", so that the agent is latent, explained by «مَثَلاً», and «مَثَلُ القومِ» is the one specified for blame, the relative noun being a ṣifa of it, and the tamyīz omitted. Sībawayh and his followers do not permit this at all; they stated explicitly that omitting the tamyīz is impermissible, and how could it be omitted when it is what clarifies?

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ}: it stands in the place of the two objects, or the one object, depending on the disagreement. And «لله» is attached to «أَوْلياء», or to an omitted element as a naʿt of «أولياء»; and {مِن دُونِ الناس} likewise.
And His saying {فَتَمَنَّوُاْ الموت} is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The majority read it with ḍamma on the wāw, which is the original for the wāw of the pronoun. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, Ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with kasra, which is the original in the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ also read it with fatḥa, which is a seeking of lightness, and the like of it was given in His saying {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16]. Al-Kisāʾī reported the substitution of a hamza for the wāw.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَتَمَنَّونَهُ}: and He said in [Sūrat] al-Baqara «ولن يتمنَّوْه». Al-Zamakhsharī [spelled in the source "al-Zamshkhasharī"] said: "There is no difference between «لا» and «لن» in that each of them is a negation of the future, except that «لن» contains an emphasis and intensity that «لا» does not; so once He used the wording of emphasis, «ولن يتمنَّوْه», and once without its wording, «ولا يتمنَّوْنه»." The Shaykh said: "This is a retraction on his part of his position, namely that «لن» requires negation in perpetuity, in favour of the position of the group, namely that it does not require it." I say: there is no retraction in it; the most that can be said is that he was silent about it. His joining «لا» and «لن» in negating the future does not rule out «لن» being distinguished by another meaning. This discussion has already been given more fully in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ}: there are two possibilities regarding the fāʾ. The first is that it enters because of the sense of condition (sharṭ) that the noun implies, and the ruling for what is described by a relative noun is the ruling for the relative noun in that respect. The second is that it is purely redundant (mazīda), not for the implication mentioned. These people invalidated the first view on two grounds. One is that this is permissible only when the mubtadaʾ or the noun of «إنَّ» is a relative noun, and the noun of «إنَّ» here is not a relative noun but is described by a relative noun. The other is that fleeing from death does not save from it, so it does not resemble a condition; he means that it is certain, so it does not resemble the condition, whose nature is to be uncertain.
The first was answered by saying that what is described, together with its description, is like one thing, and that «الذي» is only ever a qualifier; so when the thing described is not mentioned the fāʾ enters, the described being intended, and likewise when it is stated explicitly. The second was answered by saying that a great many people suppose that fleeing from the causes of death will save them till another time. Makkī allowed that the khabar be His saying {الذي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ}, with the fāʾ introducing the answer to the clause. He said: "As you say: «زيدٌ منطلقٌ فقُمْ إليه»." There is room for objection, because there is no sequence between His saying {إِنَّ المَوْتَ الذي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ} and His saying {فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ}, so it is not a parallel to what he gave as example.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إنه» without a fāʾ, and there are several possibilities concerning it. The first is that it is resumptive, and then the khabar is the relative noun itself, as if it were said: "Death is the thing that you flee from"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second is that the khabar is the clause «إنَّه مُلاقيكم», and then the relative noun is a naʿt of «الموت». The third is that «إنَّه» is an emphasis; since the speech about death became long, the particle was emphasized with verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī). You know that it is emphasized in this way only by repeating what it governed, or by repeating its pronoun; so it was emphasized by repeating the pronoun of what «إنَّ» had entered. Then the relative noun is a naʿt of «الموت», and «مُلاقِيكم» is its khabar, as if it were said: «إنَّ الموتَ إنَّه مُلاقيكم».

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {مِن يَوْمِ الجمعة}: this «مِنْ» is a clarification (bayān) of «إذا» and an explanation of it; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: it is in the sense of «في», that is, "on the day". The majority read «الجمعة» with two ḍammas. Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read it with sukūn on the mīm. It was said: it is a dialectal variant of the first and was made quiescent for lightness, being the dialect of Tamīm. It was also said: it is a maṣdar in the sense of gathering (ijtimāʿ). It was also said: since it is in the sense of the act, it became like رجل هُزْأَة, that is, a man who is mocked; so when al-jumʿa has the sense of gathering, it was made quiescent, because it is a direct object in meaning, or resembles it, and so it became like هُزْأَة, he who is mocked. Makkī said this; Abū l-Baqāʾ likewise said: "It is in the sense of 'that in which people gather', like رجل ضُحْكَة, that is, one who is laughed at." Makkī said: "Making the mīm quiescent is permissible for lightness. It was also said that it is a dialect." I say: it has been given that it is a reading, and that it is the dialect of Tamīm. The Shaykh said: "There is also a dialect with fatḥa which has not been read." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it as a reading, saying: "It is read with fatḥa on the mīm in the sense of the agent, that is, the day of the place that gathers, like رجلٌ ضُحْكَة, that is, one who laughs much." Makkī said something close to it, for he said: "And there is a third dialect with fatḥa on the mīm, attributing the act to it, as if it gathers the people, as one says رجلٌ لُحَنَة if he often corrects people's grammar, and قُرَأَة if he often teaches people to recite." Al-Zamakhsharī also reported it as a reading, except that he made «الجُمْعة» with sukūn the original and the one with ḍamma a lightened form of it [as written]; he said: "يوم الجُمعة is the day of the gathered crowd, like their saying ضُحْكَة for one laughed at. And يوم الجُمعة with fatḥa on the mīm is the day of the time that gathers, like their saying ضُحَكة and لُعَبة; and يوم الجُمُعة is a heavier form of الجُمْعَة, as عُسُرة was said for عُسْرة. And it has been read with all of them." [Translator's note: the text as printed describes the ḍamma form as "lightened" and then the heavier form as a thickening; it is translated as written.] His implied form "the day of the time that gathers" is better than Abū l-Baqāʾ's "the day of the place that gathers", because attributing gathering to the two adverbials is figurative, so it is preferable to keep it as time, in its state.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {انفضوا إِلَيْهَا}: He returned the pronoun to the commerce rather than the diversion, because it is the more important of the cause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He said «إليها» and did not say «إليهما» out of concern for the more important, since it was the cause of the diversion, and the diversion was not its cause. And consider that commerce was put before diversion in the sighting because it is more important, and was put after it in the preference, so that the soul first lights upon the clearer." End. In his saying "He did not say «إليهما»" and then answering as he did there is an objection that is not hidden; for with a conjunction by «أو» the pronoun, the khabar, the ḥāl and the qualifier are not put in the dual, because it is for one of the two things; for that reason people interpreted «إنْ يكُنْ غنياً أو فقيراً فاللَّهُ أَوْلى بهما» as I set out in its place. The answer to it is only that He put the pronoun in the singular because the conjunction is by «أو». And the pronoun of the commerce was brought, rather than the pronoun of the diversion, though the latter would be permissible, for what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned in answer, which is the fact of its being the more important, as more than one has said. Al-Zamakhsharī too said something close to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, for he said: "How did He say «إليها» when He has mentioned two things? I say: its implied form is: when they saw commerce they dispersed to it, or a diversion they dispersed to it; so one was omitted because the mentioned one indicates it, and likewise the reading of those who read «انفَضُّوا إليه»." End. His saying "I say: its implied form..." to the end suggests that the proper form of the speech was that the pronoun be dual, but it was omitted. In it is what I set before you: that what prevents this is a technical matter, namely the conjunction by «أو».
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «إليه», returning the pronoun to the diversion; al-Akhfash expressly allowed that on the basis of hearing it from the Arabs, for example: «إذا جاءك زيد أو هند فأَكْرِمه», and if you wish «فأكرِمْها». Some read «إليهما» in the dual. Its explanation is like the explanation of {إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقِيراً} [al-Nisāʾ: 135], whose treatment has been given.
His saying: {وَتَرَكُوكَ}: a circumstantial clause from the agent of «انفَضُّوا», with «قد» implied in the view of some. And His saying {مَا عِندَ الله خَيْرٌ}: «ما» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and «خيرٌ» is its khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ (١))
His saying (الْمَلِكِ): it and what follows it are read in the genitive as naʿt (adjective), and in the nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf). The majority read the qāf of «الْقُدُّوسِ» with ḍamma, and it has been read with fatḥa; they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَائِمًا. . . (١١))
His saying (إِلَيْهَا): the pronoun was made feminine only because He referred it back to the merchandise (التِّجَارَة), since that was more important to them. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣))
His saying (وَآخَرِينَ): it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الْأُمِّيِّين.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْرَاةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ الْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًا بِئْسَ مَثَلُ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٥))
His saying (يَحْمِلُ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْحِمَارِ», and what governs it is the meaning of الْمَثَل (likeness).
His saying (بِئْسَ مَثَلُ): this «مَثَلُ» is the fāʿil (agent) of بِئْسَ. On «الَّذِينَ» there are two views.
The first: it is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الْقَوْم, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "this likeness". The second: it is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "evil is the likeness of the people: the likeness of those who…"; so the omitted مَثَل is the one specified for blame; it was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ إِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ. . . (٨))
His saying (فَإِنَّهُ مُلَاقِيكُمْ): the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and the fāʾ entered because of the resemblance of «الَّذِي» to a condition. Some disallowed this, saying: this is permissible only when الَّذِي is the mubtadaʾ (subject) or the noun of إِنَّ, whereas الَّذِي here is an adjective (ṣifa). They also weakened it from another angle, namely that fleeing from death does not save from it, so it does not resemble a condition; these people said: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).
This has been answered: the adjective and the described noun are like a single thing; and since «الَّذِي» can only be an adjective, when the described noun is not mentioned with it the fāʾ enters while the described noun is intended, so it is likewise when it is stated explicitly. As for what they mentioned second, it is not correct, for a great many people think that fleeing from the causes of death will save them until another time.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٩))
His saying (مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ): «مِنْ» is in the sense of فِي (on). And الْجُمُعَة, with two ḍammas and with the mīm vowelless [الْجُمْعَة], is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of الِاجْتِمَاع (gathering). It is also said of the form with the vowelless mīm: it is in the sense of "that in which people gather", like رَجُلٌ ضُحْكَةٌ, i.e. one who is laughed at.
It is also read with fatḥa on the mīm [الْجُمَعَة], in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "the day of the place that gathers", like رَجُلٌ ضُحَكَةٌ, i.e. one who laughs a lot.
«[Translator's note: the source has «فِي الْمَسْكَنِ» ("in the dwelling"), evidently a corruption of «فِي الْمُسَكَّنِ» ("of the vowelless form"); translated in the latter sense.]»

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Jumuʿa (Friday)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿المَلِكِ القُدُّوسِ﴾ — the reading is with a ḍamma on the qāf. It has also been transmitted as ”اَلقَدُّوسُ“ with a fatḥa on the qāf, but that is rare. The meaning of ”اَلْقُدُّوسُ“ is: the Blessed; and it is also said: the Pure.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ في الأُمِّيِّينَ رَسُولا مِنهُمْ﴾ — ”اَلْأُمِّيِّينَ“ are those who do not write, who are as the community (umma) was created before learning writing; and writing comes only through learning. Likewise their saying of one who knows neither (grammatical) speech nor reading: ”هُوَ يَقْرَأُ بِالسَّلِيقَةِ“ (he reads by natural disposition), i.e. he did not learn the Quran with its iʿrāb (case-endings) but reads according to how he heard speech, by his natural disposition. ”اَلسَّلِيقَةُ“, ”اَلطَّبِيعَةُ“, ”اَلنَّحِيبَةُ“, ”اَلسَّجِيَّةُ“ and ”اَلسَّرْجُوجَةُ“ all mean: natural disposition. [Translator's note: النحيبة is so printed; the word usually listed among these synonyms is النَّحِيتة.] It is said that writing first began among the Arabs from the people of al-Ṭāʾif; the people of al-Ṭāʾif mentioned that they learned writing among the people of al-Ḥīra, and the people of al-Ḥīra mentioned that they learned writing from the people of al-Anbār.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مِنهم لَمّا يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ﴾ — ”آخَرِينَ“ is in the position of the genitive. The meaning is: "He it is who sent among the unlettered a messenger from among them, and sent (him) among those who have not yet joined them," i.e. among others of them who have not yet joined them. So the Prophet ﷺ is sent to those who saw him and to everyone who came after them, of the Arabs and the non-Arabs. It is also possible for ﴿وَآخَرِينَ﴾ to be in the position of the accusative, in the sense: "He teaches them the Book and wisdom, and teaches others of them who have not yet joined them."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْراةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوها كَمَثَلِ الحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أسْفارًا﴾ — ”اَلْأسْفارُ“ are large books; its singular is ”سِفْرٌ“. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the likeness of the Jews, in their abandoning the application of the Torah and belief in the Prophet ﷺ whom they find written with them in it, is as the likeness of a donkey carrying volumes. Then He said: ﴿بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ﴾, and the meaning of ﴿بِئْسَ مَثَلُ القَوْمِ﴾ is: "the likeness which We have struck for them." Abū ʿAmr read ”كَمَثَلِ الحِمِارِ“ with kasra of the alif; and this imāla (inclination) — I mean the kasra of the rāʾ — is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.

His saying: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ means: He does not guide one of whom it is already in His knowledge that he will be a wrongdoer.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ هادُوا إنْ زَعَمْتُمْ أنَّكم أوْلِياءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ النّاسِ﴾ — that is because they said: ﴿نَحْنُ أبْناءُ اللَّهِ وأحِبّاؤُهُ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 18]. So it was said to them: if you claim (that), ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا المَوْتَ﴾, i.e. for Allah will cause you to die. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that they would not wish for it, because they knew that the Prophet ﷺ is true and that if they wished for it they would die; so they did not wish for it. This is among the most telling of the signs of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:8-8.t: Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that even if they did not wish for death and did not die at that time, they would die without doubt, and He said: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ المَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنهُ فَإنَّهُ مُلاقِيكُمْ﴾. The fāʾ has entered the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“, though ”إنَّ زَيْدًا فَمُنْطَلِقٌ“ is not permissible, because in ﴿الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنهُ فَإنَّهُ مُلاقِيكُمْ﴾ there is the sense of condition and requital. It is also possible that the sentence is complete at ﴿قُلْ إنَّ المَوْتَ الَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنهُ﴾, as though it were said: "If you flee from any death whatever, by killing or otherwise, it will meet you," and ﴿فَإنَّهُ﴾ is then a fresh start (istiʾnāf) after the first predicate.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاةِ مِن يَوْمِ الجُمُعَةِ﴾ — it was also read ”اَلْجُمْعَةِ“ with the mīm quiescent. ”اَلْجُمَعَةِ“ with a fatḥa on the mīm is permissible in the language, but it ought not to be recited unless a transmission of it from one of the imams of the readers is established. Whoever read ”اَلْجُمْعَةِ“, that is a lightening of ”اَلْجُمُعَةِ“ because of the heaviness of the two ḍammas. And whoever says, outside recitation, ”اَلْجُمَعَةِ“, its meaning is: the one that gathers people, just as you say ”رَجُلٌ لُعَنَةٌ“, i.e. one who curses people a great deal, and ”رَجُلٌ ضُحَكَةٌ“, one who laughs a great deal.

His saying: ﴿فاسْعَوْا إلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ means: proceed to the remembrance of Allah; it does not mean running. Ibn Masʿūd read ”فامْضُوا إلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ“ and said: "If it were 'fa-sʿaw' (hasten), I would hasten until my cloak fell off." Ubayy ibn Kaʿb likewise read ”فامْضُوا“, and it has been transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; but following the muṣḥaf is more proper, and had ”فامْضُوا“ alone been (the reading) with ʿUmar, he would have changed it in the muṣḥaf. The proof that the meaning of ”اَلسَّعْيُ“ is engaging in any work is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأنْ لَيْسَ لِلإنْسانِ إلا ما سَعى﴾ [al-Najm: 39] ﴿وَأنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرى﴾ [al-Najm: 40]; there is no disagreement that its meaning is: "and that man has nothing but what he has worked for."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَذَرُوا البَيْعَ ذَلِكم خَيْرٌ لَكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — so selling, from the time the sun passes the meridian on Friday until the prayer is finished, is as something forbidden.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فانْتَشِرُوا في الأرْضِ وابْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — this means permission; it does not mean "when the prayer is finished a person must trade," just as He said: ﴿وَإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾ [al-Māʾida: 2]: it is not obligatory on one who has left the state of iḥrām to hunt; it is only permitted to him. Like that is one's saying in ordinary speech: "When you are in my presence, do not speak; and when you are away from me, say what you wish" — it only means permission.

His saying: ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا المَوْتَ﴾ [al-Jumuʿa: 6] — with a ḍamma on the wāw because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām. The ḍamma was chosen with the wāw because the original vowel of the wāw here is the nominative (rafʿ), since it stands for nominative nouns. It was also read ”فَتَمَنَّوِ المَوْتَ“ with a kasra on the wāw, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: when they meet across two words, the first of them takes kasra, as you say ”قَلِ الحَقَّ“, giving the lām a kasra because of the quiescence of the lām of ”اَلْحَقَّ“. [Translator's note: so printed; the imperative is قُلِ الحقَّ.]

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا رَأوْا تِجارَةً أوْ لَهْوًا انْفَضُّوا إلَيْها﴾ — He did not say ”إلَيْهِما“ (to the two of them). It is permissible in speech to say: "And when they see trade or amusement, they scatter to it (ilayhi), they scatter to it (ilayhā), and they scatter to them both (ilayhimā)." The predicate of one of the two has been omitted because the second predicate indicates the omitted predicate; the meaning is: "When they see trade they scatter to it, or amusement they scatter to it." It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ was giving his sermon when camels belonging to Diḥya ibn Khalīfa al-Kalbī arrived carrying oil, and they scattered to look at them and left the Prophet ﷺ preaching; the Prophet ﷺ remained with twelve men, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Had the last of them followed the first of them, the valley would have blazed with fire."» So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that what is with Allah is better than amusement and than trade, and the Prophet ﷺ made known how grave it is to turn away from the imam while he is preaching on Friday. "Amusement" (”اَللَّهْوُ“) here is said to be the drum; and it is — Allah knows best — anything with which one is diverted.

﴿واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرّازِقِينَ﴾ means: nothing of their provision escapes them because they stayed behind from looking at the provisions caravan, nor because they left off selling at the time of the prayer and the sermon.
